approachQuestion.prompt:
Successor Walk. Return the IDs of all nodes in left-subtree, node, right-subtree order. This tree representation includes a correct parent pointer at every node; the root parent is null. The input supplies a writable output array of length n and the root pointer. Fill the array without modifying any pointers.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 4(9(-,2(-,-)),7(-,-)). Output: [9,2,4,7]. Example 2: Input: 8(3(1(-,-),-),-). Output: [1,3,8]. Example 3: Input: -. Output: []. Parent links point back to the displayed parents and are omitted in the notation.

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; IDs are unique signed 32-bit integers and have no ordering promise. Child pointers form one valid tree with no shared nodes or cycles. Parent pointers are consistent and already supplied as part of input. Shape is unrestricted; the output buffer is reserved only for final IDs.

options.text: Start at the leftmost node. Emit it, then repeatedly take its inorder successor: descend to the leftmost node of a right subtree when one exists; otherwise climb parent pointers until leaving a left child, then use that parent. Stop when no successor exists.
options.feedback: Parent links identify the next unfinished ancestor without a stored stack. Every node has exactly one position in the requested order.

options.text: Ignore the parent pointers and use a standard explicit ancestor stack to emit the left-node-right traversal into the output.
options.feedback: The order is correct for every input, but the supplied parent links can replace this extra ancestor storage entirely.

options.text: After emitting a node with no right child, always emit its immediate parent next, unless that parent is null.
options.feedback: In Example 1, after node 2 its immediate parent 9 has already been emitted. The next node is 4, reached by climbing past the right-child link.

options.text: Emit the root first, then its entire left subtree and then its entire right subtree.
options.feedback: Example 1 begins with 9, not root 4. Root-first traversal uses a different order.

feedback.reason: Parent pointers replace an ancestor stack, and the cost of many upward moves is amortized over edges.
details: Find the leftmost node and emit it. If it has a right child, find that subtree’s leftmost node. Otherwise climb while the current node is a right child; the first parent reached from a left child is next. If the climb reaches null, finish. Repeat, storing only current and temporary pointers plus the output index.

Parent pointers replace an explicit ancestor stack. One successor step can climb far, but across the full walk each edge is traversed only a bounded number of times. Summing h per node would overcount those shared climbs.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze the entire revealed successor walk for n>=1 nodes. Let h be the tree height. What is the tight worst-case pair for producing all n IDs? Include the initial leftmost descent and all parent climbs; count temporary pointers and index. Exclude input parent/child links and the supplied final output buffer. Each pointer step and output write takes constant time; no recursion or auxiliary stack is used.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer steps, comparison of node identity, and output writes take constant time. Analyze the total worst-case cost of the entire walk, counting all repeated climbs; parent pointers are input, not auxiliary allocations. No hashing, recursion, copying, or dynamic-array resizing is used.

feedback.reason: Whole-walk edge accounting gives linear time with fixed pointer storage.
details: Across the whole walk every child edge is traversed at most once downward and once upward, and n IDs are emitted. Only a fixed number of pointers and an index are retained.

A right subtree supplies the next ID when present. Otherwise, ancestors already exited through their right child are complete; the first ancestor reached from a left child is next. This generates each inorder successor exactly once.

“O(nh) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: One successor search may climb h links, but those long climbs cannot occur independently for every node. Across the full walk each child edge is descended and climbed at most once.

“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Across the whole walk every child edge is traversed at most once downward and once upward, and n IDs are emitted. Only a fixed number of pointers and an index are retained.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: A stack would use height-dependent memory, but the supplied parent pointers already provide the return route and are excluded as input.
“O(h) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The walk must emit all n IDs; a wide tree may have many more nodes than height.
